title: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner (CLF-C02) Hands-On Lab & Cloud Foundation Architecture
problem: Aspiring cloud engineers and developers studying for the AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner (CLF-C02) exam often rely on passive flashcard memorization and rote multiple-choice dumps without understanding how core AWS infrastructure operates in code. Consequently, while they may pass an introductory exam, they remain unable to configure secure IAM least-privilege permission boundaries, architect multi-tier VPC network isolation, or implement cost-optimization alerts on cloud infrastructure. This guide delivers a hands-on lab preparation curriculum and reproducible infrastructure project in LocalStack and AWS. The engineer constructs an IAM least-privilege role matrix, provisions a multi-tier VPC with public and private subnets hosting EC2 and S3 static assets, configures automated CloudWatch billing alarms, and verifies architectural best practices against the AWS Well-Architected Framework.

use_cases.title: IAM Least-Privilege Identity & Access Management Governance
use_cases.first_sentence: Enterprise organizations migrating workloads to the public cloud must enforce role-based access control and prevent root account credential usage.
use_cases.second_sentence: The engineer configures granular IAM policies with permission boundaries, enforces Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), and verifies programmatic access restriction across administrative roles.

use_cases.title: Multi-Tier Web Architecture with S3 Static Hosting & EC2 Compute
use_cases.first_sentence: Companies hosting customer-facing digital web portals need scalable, highly available web tiers isolated from public database tiers.
use_cases.second_sentence: The lab provisions an isolated VPC with public subnets for Application Load Balancers and private subnets for compute instances, serving static assets via Amazon S3.

use_cases.title: Cloud Financial Management & Automated Cost Budget Alerting
use_cases.first_sentence: Startups and corporate teams running on cloud infrastructure must prevent unexpected billing overruns caused by orphaned resources or traffic spikes.
use_cases.second_sentence: The project sets up AWS Budgets and CloudWatch alarm metrics that trigger notification alerts when simulated monthly spending exceeds configured monetary thresholds.

hard_parts: Translating the AWS Shared Responsibility Model into concrete IAM JSON policies and security group inbound/outbound rules
Designing multi-tier VPC network routing tables, Internet Gateways (IGW), and CIDR block allocations in software-defined networks
Configuring CloudWatch billing alarm metrics and AWS Budget triggers with automated notification delivery mechanisms
Executing local cloud emulation via LocalStack to validate AWS CLI commands and API operations without incurring cloud billing costs
screener_signals: Clean infrastructure repository containing documented IAM policies, VPC network configuration templates, and CloudWatch alarm scripts
Security verification report proving 50 of 50 unauthorized IAM API actions are blocked with AccessDenied exceptions
Anti-fake verification script creating an IAM user without S3 permissions and asserting immediate HTTP 403 AccessDenied rejection upon bucket access

architecture.data_flow: An administrator authenticates via AWS CLI with role credentials; the IAM engine evaluates permission boundaries; upon authorization, the operator provisions an AWS VPC with public and private subnets; static assets are synced to Amazon S3 with restricted bucket policies; compute workloads launch in private subnets behind security groups; CloudWatch continuously collects metric logs; when a simulated billing event exceeds the budget threshold, CloudWatch fires an alarm notification; LocalStack emulates all AWS API interactions locally for zero-cost verification.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Cryptographic AWS Signature Version 4 (SigV4) authentication and strict JSON policy evaluation returning HTTP 403 on violations.

targets.metric: IAM Least-Privilege Permission Boundary Enforcement Rate
targets.method: Percentage of unauthorized API requests blocked with AccessDenied when executed by restricted IAM role
targets.input: 50 simulated AWS CLI API calls targeting unauthorized S3 and EC2 actions across restricted roles
targets.environment: LocalStack local AWS emulation container running IAM service emulator
targets.minimum_pass: 50 of 50 unauthorized API calls rejected with HTTP 403 AccessDenied
targets.target: 50 of 50 unauthorized API calls rejected with HTTP 403 AccessDenied
targets.report: IAM security evaluation report and access rejection audit log

targets.method: Round-trip network ping latency between public subnet gateway and private subnet compute instance
targets.input: 100 ICMP network packets transmitted across virtual subnet boundaries
targets.environment: Local software-defined VPC network topology in LocalStack / Docker
targets.minimum_pass: Average packet latency is < 20 milliseconds with 0 packet loss
targets.target: Average packet latency is < 8 milliseconds with 0 packet loss
targets.report: VPC network routing latency report and routing table configuration trace

targets.metric: Automated CloudWatch Billing Budget Threshold Alert Latency
targets.method: Elapsed time from simulated budget overrun event injection to CloudWatch alarm state transition and notification dispatch
targets.input: Simulated $15 spend metric injected into CloudWatch metric stream with $10 budget threshold
targets.environment: LocalStack CloudWatch and SNS mock service environment
targets.minimum_pass: Alarm triggers and dispatches notification within 60 seconds
targets.target: Alarm triggers and dispatches notification within 25 seconds
targets.report: CloudWatch alarm event log and notification delivery timestamp summary
